stories.headline: US Air Force pulls bombers from UK air base after suspected terror attack
stories.title: US Air Force pulls bombers from UK air base after suspected terror attack
stories.summary: The US Air Force has brought home its bombers stationed at a US-run military air base in England used to strike Iran following an investigation into a planned terror attack at the RAF Fairford base. The bombers were redeployed back to their home bases in the United States, according to a Pentagon official who was not authorized to discuss sensitive military movements and spoke Sunday on condition of anonymity. Aviation watchers such as the Military Air Tracking Alliance have observed dozens of B-52 and B-1 bombers operating out of RAF Fairford since the opening days of the Iran war. Observers noticed a host of B-1 bombers fly out of the base on Sunday. The move comes as President Donald Trump weighs options for his war on Iran - including new strikes - despite his initial promises to Americans that the campaign would last a matter of weeks. "We have decisions that I'll make about Iran. Iran's been decimated. So the only question is - it'll either be the easy way, or the hard way,"

stories.headline: India seeks bigger role in effort to end the Russia-Ukraine War
stories.title: India seeks bigger role in effort to end the Russia-Ukraine War
stories.summary: The comments point to a more active role for New Delhi after years of taking a cautious approach to the war, in part because of its longstanding ties with Russia
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: India is taking a more direct role in efforts to end the conflict between Russia and Ukraine, engaging both sides on issues, including shipping and reducing hostilities, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said.

Speaking at a security conference over the weekend, Jaishankar said India in recent months has become “a little bit more involved beyond advocacy.” The comments point to a more active role for New Delhi after years of taking a cautious approach to the war, in part because of its longstanding ties with Russia.
“We have conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard.
We are trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue,” he said, adding that talks have also covered energy shipments and “non-attack possibilities.”
India has called for a halt to the fighting but has been reluctant to criticize the Kremlin, abstaining from United Nations votes condemning the war.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi called on Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the conflict during a meeting on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Kyrgyzstan in late August.
Jaishankar said dialogue and diplomacy are essential to ending the war.
He added that India’s relationship with Russia has evolved over the years and now spans energy, space and trade.

When Modi met Putin on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in September, the two pledged to deepen ties, underscoring their close relationship even as Washington pressed New Delhi to distance itself from Moscow.
The US has sought to use its position as India’s top trading partner to pressure New Delhi to stop buying Russian oil.
India’s purchases initially declined before picking up again during the Middle East war.
Russia is also a major supplier of weapons to New Delhi.

stories.headline: SI suspended for pointing pistol at flood victim during distribution of relief materials in Bihar’s Saran
stories.title: SI suspended for pointing pistol at flood victim during distribution of relief materials in Bihar’s Saran
stories.summary: The State government has also suspended seven engineers and initiated departmental proceedings against another official for alleged negligence in handling floods
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A Sub-Inspector and Station House Officer (SHO) of Maker.
Police Station in Saran district has been suspended for pointing a gun at the flood victims during the distribution of relief materials.
The video of a SHO pointing a gun and showing footwear to the flood victims went viral on social media.
The incident happened on Sunday (October 4, 2026) afternoon near Reva Ghat.
Late at night, around 11 p.m., Saran Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Roshan Kumar issued the suspension order.

“A video is circulating on various social media platforms showing Sub-Inspector Sangram Kumar Singh, Station House Officer (SHO) of Maker, pointing his pistol at the public during the distribution of flood relief materials; prima facie, this conduct reflects gross negligence in the discharge of his duties, indiscipline, and arbitrary behaviour,” SSP Roshan said in the press statement.
He added, “For the negligence displayed, Sub-Inspector Sangram Kumar Singh, SHO of Maker Police Station, is hereby suspended with immediate effect and placed on subsistence allowance.
During suspension, he will be designated at headquarters.
Subsistence allowance will be payable subject to his attendance.”
In the video, the SI is seen standing on top of a pickup truck loaded with rations and arguing with flood-affected villagers lined up for relief material.
Some villagers just stepped out of line to grab rations when the SI first flashed his footwear and then pulled out his gun, aiming it at the flood victims.

The Opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) attacked the State government over the incident by posting a message on the social media account X along with the video of the SI, asserting that those in power are treating common people like insects.

stories.title: Swastikam distributes study materials to 1,280 flood-affected students of Upper Assam
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: KOKRAJHAR: Swastikam NGO distributed study materials to 1,280 students across several government schools in flood-affected areas of Upper Assam to support children whose education was disrupted by the Assam floods.
Swastikam founder-trustee Anamika Basumatary said the initiative was undertaken as part of the NGO’s Assam Flood Relief programme.

An online and social media donation campaign was launched to mobilise support for affected children, receiving contributions from individuals, organisations and well-wishers from across the country and abroad.
Roaring Bodoland contributed more than 300 study kits for flood-affected students.
Basumatary expressed gratitude to the organisation for supporting the educational relief initiative.
She said former students of Notre Dame Academy, Munger and Jamalpur, also made a substantial financial contribution, helping the NGO reach more students and provide essential educational materials.
Basumatary also thanked BKWAC Executive Member Binod Basumatary and UBPO president Manuranjan Basumatary for joining the distribution drive.
She expressed appreciation to Ritesh Kumar and Shravan Kumar Sinha, who travelled from Bihar to participate in the relief and educational support initiative.
The initiative was aimed at ensuring continuity of education for children affected by the floods.
While flood-affected families face challenges related to food, shelter and livelihoods, the educational needs of children can often be overlooked.
The distribution of study materials sought to provide immediate support and encourage students to resume their studies with confidence.

stories.headline: Trump wrongly cites Indian election to call US voting process ‘corrupt’
stories.title: Trump wrongly cites Indian election to call US voting process ‘corrupt’
stories.summary: Washington, Oct 5 : In an apparent faux pas, US President Donald Trump mentioned India in a social media post to claim that the electoral process in the US was "corrupt", when there were no elections in India, and the post clearly appeared to be about the presidential election in Brazil. In a Truth Social post on Sunday, Trump claimed that "125 million people voted in India's Presidential elections and the results came out shortly after the vote closed". "Voting in America is CORRUPT," Trump said, referring to the weeks taken for the counting of votes in elections in US cities and states. "125 Million People voted today in the first round of India's Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the SAME DAY," Trump said. "In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is CORRUPT," the US president said. The reference to India appeared to be a possible mix-up with Brazil. Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with 125.27 million valid votes recorded, according to the country's electoral authority. Results began to be released at 5 pm, when voting ended, and were updated as ballots were received and processed. Brazilians voted in the presidential election pitting incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. With neither of them able to secure a majority in the first round, the run-off election will be held on October 25. India, meanwhile, did not hold a presidential election. President Droupadi Murmu, who took office in July 2022, is the current President of India. Also, Indians do not directly elect their President. The President is elected by an Electoral College comprising elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of the legislative assemblies of the states and union territories through a system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote. In India's regular elections, voters directly elect members of the Lok Sabha (lower house of the Parliament) and state legislative assemblies. The Prime Minister is then appointed by the President, usually the leader of the party or coalition commanding a majority in the Lok Sabha, while chief ministers are appointed by state governors, usually the leader of the party or coalition commanding a majority in the state assembly. India had nearly 980 million registered electors in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. Trump has previously cited Indian elections, particularly the country's voter identification system, to push for electoral reforms in the US. In August, Trump said India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had spoken with officials from his administration and asked how US elections can be held without a valid photo identification card. The US president made these remarks to drum up support for the SAVE America Act, which would require Americans to show proof of citizenship to register to vote, impose a nationwide voter identification requirement and severely limit voting by mail. "Earlier this month, India's Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, asked our Administration â€" How can you have Elections in the US without a valid Photo ID," Trump said on August 17. "India's last Election had 646,000,000 Voters! Less than one per cent voted by mail, and every single Voter had to have a VALID Photo Identity Document." "We need to pass THE SAVE AMERICA ACT, now," he had then asserted in a social media post. PTI

stories.headline: SIR, an Election Commission process to remove dead, false voters: Telangana BJP chief
stories.title: SIR, an Election Commission process to remove dead, false voters: Telangana BJP chief
stories.summary: Rao said, “AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and other leaders who are opposing the SIR process should know that it is initiated by the Election Commission of India, and not the BJP.”
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Rao said, “AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and other leaders who are opposing the SIR process should know that it is initiated by the Election Commission of India, and not the BJP.”

Hyderabad: Hitting out at the Opposition for allegedly misleading the masses, Telangana BJP President R. Rao said that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is not done by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) but by the Election Commission of India (ECI), and that it was just a process to remove fake and dead voters from the voters' list.
He added that the process was also done during the Congress' rule, but it was not opposed then.
Rao said, “Owaisi and other leaders who are opposing SIR should know that it is a process not introduced by the BJP.
It is an Election Commission process.
It was also carried out during the Congress' rule.
They did not oppose it then, so why are they opposing it now?”
He said, “Even in Keralam, Congress won after SIR, but they have no answer for it.
Whenever the Congress or the INDIA Bloc loses elections, they blame either the Election Commission of India or EVMs.”

He added, “Owaisi and Congress are frustrated because the BJP has been in power for the last 12 years, and it appears that it will continue to be in power, because people have lost faith in the Congress and the INDIA Bloc.”

He also said, “Therefore, Congress and Owaisi are trying to mislead the people about SIR, which is a process to delete voters who are dead, duplicate voters, or foreigners, and it is also a process where, if people are residing elsewhere, their votes must be shifted there; this is what SIR is.
So there is no illegality; there is nothing to object to; there should be no objection in this regard.”

stories.headline: Gyanesh Kumar undermined Election Commission’s independence: Sachin Pilot
stories.title: Gyanesh Kumar undermined Election Commission’s independence: Sachin Pilot
stories.summary: Congress leader Sachin Pilot alleged the SIR is being used to selectively delete voters, as he also criticised the Rajasthan government’s drought response and the AAP government in Punjab
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Congress leader Sachin Pilot on Sunday (October 4, 2026) accused Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar of undermining the independence of the Election Commission, alleging that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was being used to selectively delete voters.

Talking to reporters in Jaipur, Mr. Pilot alleged that Mr. Kumar had sidelined the other two Election Commissioners while taking decisions related to the electoral roll revision, and demanded action against him.
“India and the country function according to law.
The Election Commission has three members, and decisions are taken either unanimously or by a majority.
But Gyanesh Kumar sidelined the other two Election Commissioners and started the entire process on his own,” he alleged.
Mr. Pilot claimed that powers normally exercised by Electoral Registration.
Officers (EROs) at the local level were being centralised, and alleged that names of voters were being added or deleted from Delhi.
He claimed about 13 crore names had been removed from electoral rolls across the country, and alleged that voters were being selectively targeted in States including Haryana, Bihar and West Bengal.
“First there was demonetisation, and now they are doing ‘votebandi’.
Voting is the biggest democratic right of a citizen.
If that right is taken away, what could be more serious than this?” Mr. Pilot said.
He alleged that public confidence in the Election Commission as an impartial constitutional institution had been eroded, and demanded action against the CEC.

stories.headline: JD(U) backs Neeraj Kumar as NDA eyes sweep in Bihar MLC polls
stories.title: JD(U) backs Neeraj Kumar as NDA eyes sweep in Bihar MLC polls
stories.summary: Patna, Oct 5 : As JD(U) candidate Neeraj Kumar is set to file his nomination for the Bihar Legislative Council elections on Monday, the party expressed confidence that the NDA will win all eight seats in the upcoming biennial polls, describing the contest as a one-sided affair. The Election Commission of India (ECI) has announced October 23 as the date for the biennial elections to eight seats of the Bihar Legislative Council. JD(U) Bihar president Umesh Kushwaha said the NDA would secure victory on all eight seats. “The NDA will win all eight seats, and it will be a one-sided victory. No one is in contention. You know how the NDA performed in the 2025 Assembly elections. This is based on the trust of our workers, and we have placed our trust in them,” Kushwaha said. JD(U) spokesperson Rajiv Ranjan also expressed confidence in Neeraj Kumar, saying he would continue the party's winning streak. “He will continue the winning streak. The way he has consistently served the party and the people, he has also been vocal in the Legislative Council. He has been recognised as a popular leader since the party's inception, and this will undoubtedly benefit him in the Legislative Council election," he said. The election for eight seats in the Teacher and Graduate constituencies of the Legislative Council has generated considerable interest even before the nomination process. Differences have emerged within both the NDA and the Grand Alliance camps. Within the NDA, differences have surfaced in the JD(U) over the Patna Graduate constituency. At the same time, the Rashtriya Lok Morcha (RLM), a key constituent of the NDA, has reportedly expressed resentment over not being allotted a seat. The contest has also gained significance amid the ongoing war of words between JD(U) MLA from Mokama, Anant Singh, and Neeraj Kumar. Neeraj recently met JD(U) national president Nitish Kumar on Saturday and sought his blessings. The meeting is being viewed as significant ahead of the MLC election. Following the meeting, Neeraj said he would file his nomination on October 5. The internal standoff between Anant Singh and Neeraj Kumar has intensified in recent days. Anant Singh on Sunday claimed that he would ensure Neeraj's defeat in the election at all costs, even if it resulted in his expulsion from the party. Meanwhile, Bihar Health Minister and former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar's son, Nishant Kumar, urged young party workers to unite and actively campaign for Neeraj Kumar to ensure his victory. Interacting with party workers, Nishant said, “Neeraj Kumar is a dedicated and experienced party colleague with an unwavering commitment to socialist ideology. He has consistently raised public grievances and issues concerning the welfare of his constituency.” On the other hand, Anant Singh maintained that the dispute between him and Neeraj Kumar was a personal matter and not a party issue. He also cautioned that leaders considering intervening in the dispute could be making a mistake. --IANS

article_sentences: The Chief Justice commented that the Court will not indulge in a mere academic exercise.

The Supreme Court's 7-judge reference on the issue of legislative privileges vis-a-vis free speech might be disposed of as an academic issue, since the Court was informed today that the 2003 resolution of the Tamil Nadu legislative assembly, which was the trigger for the case, was withdrawn in 2004.
The reference originates from the 2003 case N. Ravi.
Speaker, Legislative Assembly, Chennai, challenging the 2003 decision taken by the Tamil Nadu assembly to sentence 5 journalists of The Hindu for articles criticising the State Government.
The matter was ultimately referred to the 7-judge bench to examine the interplay between Articles 194(3), 19(1)(a) and 21 of the Constitution.
The reference remained pending for over two decades, and the Court, in August 2026, decided to commence the hearing from October 6.

A day before the scheduled hearing of the reference, Senior Advocate Raju Ramachandran, for the State of Tamil Nadu, today informed a 3-judge bench led by CJI Surya Kant that the 2003 resolution of the Assembly was revoked in 2004 itself.
Though an affidavit was filed in the Court regarding this development, this fact was omitted to be noticed in the reference order.
Since the cause of action for the case no longer survives, the reference may have become academic, Ramachandran suggested.
Ramachandran said that he was making this mention today so that the 7-judge bench is not taken by surprise tomorrow.
Solicitor General of India Tushar Mehta also said that the issue may have become academic in the light of this information.
The Chief Justice expressed that the Court will not indulge in a mere academic exercise.

stories.headline: Supreme Court to hear pleas against CEC Gyanesh Kumar today
stories.title: Supreme Court to hear pleas against CEC Gyanesh Kumar today
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 5 : The Supreme Court will hear petitions on Monday challenging whether Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar can single-handedly exercise powers constitutionally designated for the entire multi-member poll panel. As per the cause list published on the official website of the apex court, a Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana is slated to take up the matter. The matter was mentioned before the CJI earlier on September 29 by senior advocate Vikas Singh, following which the CJI said: "List it next week." The plea seeks enforcement of the collective decision-making framework governing the ECI and a writ in the nature of quo warranto concerning the authority under which the CEC has reportedly acted in the name of the poll panel. The petition contends that Article 324 of the Constitution vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the “Commission” and not in an individual Chief Election Commissioner. It further relies on Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, which provides for collective decision-making, with matters on which there is no unanimity to be decided by majority. The plea has relied upon contemporaneous written communications and file notings attributed to Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, who allegedly recorded at least 14 objections between October 2025 and August 2026 concerning decisions and steps allegedly taken in the name of the ECI without their approval. The objections, as detailed in the petition, relate to communications and orders allegedly issued without the poll body's approval, the absence of agendas before and minutes after meetings, foreign travel undertaken without approval, changes to Form 6, access to the electoral roll database and filing of appeals before tribunals in West Bengal. The plea also refers to concerns reportedly raised by the two Election Commissioners over the "gradual centralisation of the electoral roll database", and changes in the work allocation of the poll body's IT establishment. The petitioner has sought a declaration that powers vested in the ECI under Article 324 cannot be exercised or represented as an act of the poll body except in accordance with the constitutional and statutory framework governing the Commission. The plea also seeks declaratory and mandatory directions to ensure compliance with the collective decision-making framework, besides production and preservation of relevant records concerning the disputed decisions. Meanwhile, the ECI has maintained that the reported differences between the Commissioners do not amount to an institutional "rupture" and that internal objections and written notes are established mechanisms in a multi-member constitutional body. --IANS

event term: 'repo rate' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: The Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee began its three-day meeting on Monday amid mounting expectations of an interest rate increase, as rising inflation, higher oil prices and a weakening rupee complicate the policy outlook.
The committee will announce its decision on Wednesday, 7 October.
The benchmark repo rate currently stands at 5.25 per cent, with markets watching for what could be the first increase since February 2023.
Bank of America has brought forward its forecast for a 25-basis-point hike from December to October.
It said higher energy costs, food inflation and price pressures spreading across the economy could prompt the RBI to begin withdrawing monetary support at this meeting.
SBI Research also sees the risks increasingly favouring a quarter-percentage-point increase.
Its report cited broadening inflation, deteriorating global conditions, changes in liquidity and renewed repricing of risk in financial markets as reasons for acting early.
The report argued that a pre-emptive response would be prudent given geopolitical tensions and the threat of further increases in crude prices.
Retail inflation rose to 4.82 per cent in August from 4.45 per cent in July.
Crude oil trading above $100 a barrel, rupee weakness and higher global bond yields have added to the pressures facing policymakers.
The outlook for food prices presents a further concern.
Strong El Niño conditions and the prospect of below-normal rainfall in October could affect rabi crop output, potentially adding to inflation.
